distinguishing_features: Introduces a high-permittivity dielectric filler into a capacitor dielectric defect to replace a low-permittivity void.
Uses electrostatic displacement continuity and dielectric voltage sharing to reduce local electric field.
Controls local permittivity/electric stress rather than oxide-film growth, resistivity, or chloride concentration.
Targets solid capacitor dielectric breakdown prevention rather than electrochemical anode passivation/current-efficiency restoration.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce localized electric-field amplification and partial-discharge/breakdown initiation at defects in a capacitor dielectric without globally increasing insulation thickness or dielectric grade.
parsed.viable_reason: The corrected series-dielectric calculation uses obtainable high-k filler properties and predicts the defect field drops from about 3.9 kV/mm to about 0.40 kV/mm while the bulk field remains far below polymer breakdown.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 3 only teaches pulse-dosed chloride chemistry to dissolve a passive film and provides no teaching or motivation to replace a low-permittivity dielectric defect with a high-permittivity filler to exploit displacement-continuity voltage sharing.
